stacks.crossnote:
CROSS-CHECK against slide 21 of Helpful CEJA Slides. Also on the table for a village, even though it is not in this stack:
• IEPA Office of Energy — Energy Code training and technical support, wastewater treatment plant energy assessments, Energy Efficiency Trust Fund.
• IFA Climate Bank — Energy Sovereignty Loan for community ownership, Community Resilience Hubs, Community Charging, C-PACE for private property inside the village, Enabling Upgrades for Solar, Carbon Free Schools.
• Fleet and transportation — IEPA Electric School Bus and EV Rebate, Charging Incentive Program, and IDOT's NEVI, Carbon Reduction Program, CMAQ and Competitive Freight-Port Infrastructure. Add these the moment the scope touches vehicles.
• Codes and construction — Building Energy Codes, Stretch Energy Codes, Capital Development Board stretch goals.
• Housing stock — IHDA Green Resilient Retrofit and Energy Efficiency Program, DCEO Weatherization Assistance.
• People — Energy Equity Portal, Energy Transition Navigators, Workforce Hubs, Returning Residents, Climate Works.
• Grid and rates — ICC net metering, Multi-Year Integrated Grid Plans, Equitable Energy Upgrade Program (still in rulemaking).
Non-energy capital for the same building often sits in a DCEO community development or infrastructure NOFO. Search the full DCEO grant catalog, not just the CEJA page.
stacks.first: First move: check whether the village owns its utility. If it does, GRID and the Small Utility Clean Energy Planning Grant are built only for you.
